To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genistein forms inclusion complexes with beta-cyodextrins, and the complexation phenomena can be investigated by FTIR spectroscopy.

the inclusion of genistein into cyclodextrin hosts has been demonstrated by means of UV-vis absorption spectroscopy, and that FTIR-ATIR spectroscopy has been used to study the host-guest interactions.

the formation of 1: 1 complexes of genisteinisoflavone with beta-cyclodekstrine, (2-hydroxipropyl)-beta-cyklo-dekstrin and methyl-beta-cyklo-deksrin was confirmed by phase solubility studies and FTIR-FTIR spectroscopy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the FTIR- ATR and UV-vis absorption spectroscopies to investigate the inclusion of the isoflavone genistein into the hydrophilic cavity of beta-CyD, HP-beta-CyD and Me-beta-CyD.
the characterization of the inclusion complexation of beta-CyDs with the isoflavone genistein.
the study of the interactions between the genistein molecule and three beta-CyDs, in the aim of improving the solubility, the bioavailability and the pharmacological activity of the isoflavone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusion phenomena are not so different for the three beta-CyDs, although the Me-beta-CyD is more effective than the others in the inclusion of the isoflavone.
the genistein molecule is included in the hydrophobic cavity of the macrocycles and the complexation phenomena have been confirmed.
, in the case of genistein-beta-CyD, the guest molecule is completely included into the cavity, whereas in the case of Me-beta-CyD and HP-beta-CyD the guest molecule is only partially included.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genistein is included in the beta-cyclodextins cavities with a 1:1 stoichiometry and that the host-guest interactions involve the formation of hydrogen bonds.
the inclusion of genistein in the cavity of the macrocycles occurs with the hydroxyl group of the guest in the primary side of the macrocycle and with the phenolic ring in the secondary side.

genistein is included in the cavity of beta-CyD, HP-beta-CyD and Me-beta-CyD, and that the host-guest complexation occurs by means of the hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions between the hydroxyl groups and the phenolic ring of the genistein with the hydroxyl and the primary hydroxyl groups of the cyclodextrins, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FTIR-ATRA is a powerful tool to characterize cyclodextrins complexes.
FTIR spectroscopy can be a useful tool for the study of the complexation of isoflavones by cyclodextrins.
the complexation of beta-CyD, HP-beta-CyD and Me-beta-CyD with genistein is a feasible way to improve the solubility, stability and bioavailability of this isoflavone.
